overview.executive_summary: Today’s verified candidates highlight software supply-chain compromises, active exploitation of exposed vulnerabilities, credential theft, and disruptive cyberattacks affecting retailers and technology users.

sections.heading: OVHcloud CLI releases backdoored on GitHub to steal developer secrets
sections.what_happened: Attackers compromised a contributor’s GitHub account and replaced five existing OVHcloud command-line interface releases with malware designed to steal secrets from disk. The files were available for up to 94 minutes.
sections.why_it_matters: Developers who downloaded the affected releases may have exposed credentials and other sensitive secrets.
sections.recommended_attention: Review downloads and deployments from the affected release window and rotate potentially exposed secrets.

sections.heading: Ahold Delhaize: Cyberattack affects services across US and Europe
sections.what_happened: Ahold Delhaize confirmed that a cyberattack disrupted services at stores across Europe and the United States.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident affected a major international food retailer and caused operational disruption across multiple regions.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor service restoration and any further disclosures about affected systems or data.

sections.heading: Nikkei discloses third data breach in a month, 1.8M records exposed
sections.what_happened: Nikkei disclosed a new breach involving 1.83 million personal information records, its third disclosed breach in about a month.
sections.why_it_matters: The scale and repeated nature of the disclosures raise significant concerns about personal-data exposure and ongoing security weaknesses.
sections.recommended_attention: Track affected-record notifications and any additional details about the exposed information.

sections.heading: WordPress SEO plugin Rank Math compromised to backdoor websites
sections.what_happened: Some Rank Math PRO downloads from the vendor’s official website and delivered updates contained malware that planted hidden, self-restoring backdoors in WordPress sites.
sections.why_it_matters: A trusted software channel was used to compromise websites, potentially allowing continued unauthorized access.
sections.recommended_attention: Treat sites that installed or activated affected copies as compromised and investigate for persistence.

sections.heading: F5 releases out-of-band patches for critical NGINX vulnerabilities
sections.what_happened: F5 released emergency patches for multiple NGINX web-server flaws, including three critical vulnerabilities that can allow code execution.
sections.why_it_matters: Internet-facing web servers may be exposed to severe compromise if they remain unpatched.
sections.recommended_attention: Prioritize identifying affected NGINX systems and applying the out-of-band fixes.

sections.heading: Hackers exploit SiteGuard WAF flaw to run commands as admins
sections.what_happened: Attackers are targeting an OS command-injection flaw in SiteGuard Server Edition that can let them execute commands as root or SYSTEM.
sections.why_it_matters: Successful exploitation can provide the highest level of control over affected servers.
sections.recommended_attention: Identify exposed SiteGuard deployments, apply available mitigations, and review logs for exploitation.

sections.heading: ClickFix Attackers Exploit Siemens Software Center Flaw to Deploy Remote Access Trojan
sections.what_happened: Siemens addressed a high-severity DLL sideloading vulnerability in Siemens Software Center that has been exploited in ClickFix attacks to execute malicious code.
sections.why_it_matters: The flaw is already associated with active attack activity and can run code with the application’s privileges.
sections.recommended_attention: Apply Siemens fixes and investigate systems where suspicious DLL files or ClickFix activity were observed.

sections.heading: Hackers Use New ROMULUS ClickFix Platform to Deliver LegionLoader and Other Malware
sections.what_happened: The ROMULUS platform uses fake landing pages and ClickFix-style lures to trick users into running malicious commands that deliver LegionLoader and other malware.
sections.why_it_matters: The model turns social engineering into a reusable malware-delivery service that can target unsuspecting users.
sections.recommended_attention: Strengthen user awareness around instructions to run commands and monitor for related malware activity.

sections.heading: Hackers Exploit Plex2Shell Flaws to Install Crypto Miners and Linux Proxy Backdoor
sections.what_happened: Threat actors began exploiting a chain of four Plex Media Server vulnerabilities after a proof of concept became public, deploying cryptocurrency miners and reverse-proxy software.
sections.why_it_matters: Public exploit code was quickly followed by attacks that monetize systems and establish covert network access.
sections.recommended_attention: Patch exposed Plex Media Server instances and check for miners, proxy tools, and unusual outbound activity.

sections.heading: Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Lets Attackers in Range Run Code as Root on Routers
sections.what_happened: A flaw in Broadcom Wi-Fi setup software can allow an attacker within radio range to run code as root on Broadcom-based routers without the network password or pairing.
sections.why_it_matters: Nearby attackers may gain full device control and, in one demonstrated case, read the Wi-Fi password from the router.
sections.recommended_attention: Identify affected router models and follow vendor or provider guidance for updates and exposure reduction.

sections.heading: GhostAction Attackers Plant Credential Stealer Disguised as Font in 94 GitHub Repositories
sections.what_happened: The GhostAction campaign expanded into phishing open-source developers and delivering credential-stealing malware disguised as a fake font across 94 GitHub repositories.
sections.why_it_matters: The campaign targets developer trust and can spread through repositories and seemingly ordinary project assets.
sections.recommended_attention: Audit repository changes, developer downloads, and credentials associated with affected projects.

sections.heading: OpenCode Console Breach May Have Exposed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API Keys
sections.what_happened: An intruder reached a legacy OpenCode system and may have exposed third-party artificial intelligence provider keys saved in OpenCode Console.
sections.why_it_matters: Exposed API keys can enable unauthorized use of external services and potentially affect projects that depend on them.
sections.recommended_attention: Rotate keys stored in OpenCode Console and review provider activity for suspicious usage.

tts.text: Here’s your cybersecurity news brief. The biggest theme today is trust being turned against users. OVHcloud’s command-line interface releases were replaced with malware designed to steal developer secrets, while the Rank Math search engine optimization plugin was used to backdoor WordPress sites. Ahold Delhaize reported service disruption across Europe and the United States, and Nikkei disclosed a third breach in roughly a month affecting 1.83 million records. On the vulnerability front, F5 issued emergency patches for critical NGINX flaws, attackers are exploiting a SiteGuard web application firewall issue for root access, and a Siemens Software Center flaw is being used in ClickFix attacks. New ClickFix infrastructure called ROMULUS is also delivering malware through fake instructions. Plex Media Server flaws are being exploited to install miners and proxy backdoors. A Broadcom Wi-Fi flaw may let nearby attackers take over routers as root. Finally, GhostAction is hiding credential stealers in fake fonts across GitHub repositories, and an OpenCode breach may have exposed major artificial intelligence provider API keys. Prioritize patching, credential rotation, and supply-chain review.
